question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which of the following statements about a Cat III AIF's constitutional structure is INCORRECT?

answer.text: A Cat III AIF can be constituted as a trust, LLP, company, or statutory body corporate
A Cat III AIF can be either open-ended or close-ended
A Cat III AIF scheme must have minimum corpus of INR 20 crore
A Cat III AIF CAN exceed the 1,000 investor cap by treating additional non-accredited investors as 'guests' for a limited window

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 123, AIFs may be constituted as a trust, company, LLP or body corporate; per page 125, Cat III AIFs may be either open-ended or close-ended; and per page 400, each scheme requires minimum corpus of INR 20 crore and no scheme may have more than 1,000 counted investors, with accredited investors excluded from the computation. There is no 'guest' exception, so option D is incorrect. The Trap: Options A, B and C are all textbook correct; only D is fabricated. Read negative-framed stems carefully to identify the odd-one-out. Note: The accredited-investor exclusion is the only mechanism that allows total subscribers to go beyond the 1,000-counted-investor limit per scheme.
